newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-INDIAN OPENERS FRUSTRATE SOUTH AFRICA.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-INDIAN OPENERS FRUSTRATE SOUTH AFRICA.

text.p: Solid batting by openers Nayan Mongia and Vikram Rathore enabled India to take charge on the fourth day of the third and final test against South Africa at the Wanderers on Sunday.
The pair batted through the morning session to reach 72 without loss at lunch and stretch India's lead to 161. Mongia was 35 not out and Rathore 32 not out.
Mongia gave a couple of half chances to the toiling South Africans but it was a morning when the rub of the green went the way of India.

Paul Adams could not scoop the ball up at the end of a full length dive from square-leg when Mongia had scored 14 and one run later Andrew Hudson could not gather an equally difficult chance in the gully.
The impressive South African pace attack, which tormented the Indians in the first two tests, made run-scoring difficult but they were unable to make the breakthrough.
The Indians lost the first two tests but, given some positive batting in friendlier conditions in the final two sessions, they still have a chance of a morale-boosting win here.
